result.markdown:
An analysis of roughly **200,000 checkout links** across nearly 198,000 independent websites (published in the *2026 Indie Payments Report* by Jason Zhu) provides a massive empirical look at how indie developers, solo founders, and micro-SaaS creators are monetizing.[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=On%20that%20basis%20I%20counted%20every%20seller,see%20what%20it%20sells.%20The%20short%20version%3A) 

The data reveals a dramatic shift away from traditional infrastructure toward newer developer-focused Merchants of Record (MoRs), an explosion of software and AI tooling, and unusual operational patterns among modern indie builders.

---

### 1. The Great Migration: Stripe Dominates Volume, But Newer Platforms Own AI & SaaS
While **Stripe** remains the legacy heavyweight by sheer cumulative volume (onboarding 103,000 new sellers since 2025), its profile is heavily diluted by non-software projects: only **9% of Stripe's new sellers sell software** and **7% sell AI products**. 

In contrast, newer indie-centric payment platforms and Merchants of Record—such as **Dodo Payments, Polar, and Creem**—have become the default launchpads for modern software creators:
* **Dodo Payments:** **71%** of new sellers offer software, and **29%** sell AI products.[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=Stripe%20has%20by%20far%20the%20most%20sellers,growing%20fastest%3A%20Platform.%20New%20sellers%20in%202024.)
* **Polar:** **58%** software, **27%** AI products.[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=Stripe%20has%20by%20far%20the%20most%20sellers,growing%20fastest%3A%20Platform.%20New%20sellers%20in%202024.)
* **Creem:** **65%** software, **24%** AI products.[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=Stripe%20has%20by%20far%20the%20most%20sellers,growing%20fastest%3A%20Platform.%20New%20sellers%20in%202024.)

These newer alternatives are growing rapidly because they handle complex global tax/VAT compliance out of the box (acting as the Merchant of Record) and **accept founders from regions like mainland China** where traditional Stripe onboarding is restricted.[anyway.sh](https://anyway.sh/blog/payment-platforms-for-indie-developers-2026#:~:text=A%20processor%20can%20therefore%20be%20cheaper%20at,refunds%2C%20and%20parts%20of%20the%20dispute%20workflow.)

---

### 2. The 2026 Surge in Software and AI Products
The composition of what indie developers are building has shifted aggressively toward code and AI:
* **The Software Boom:** Throughout 2025, software hovered around 6% to 8% of new checkout links. By September 2026, software's share surged to **20%** (one in every five new sellers).[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=It%20started%20climbing%20in%20March%202026%20and,sell%20ebooks%2C%20content%20or%20community%20access.%203.) 
* **AI Tooling Clustering:** AI-focused products jumped from 2% to 12% overall among new entrants, and account for up to **24%–29%** of new sellers specifically on platforms like Dodo, Polar, and Creem. 

Despite this tech-heavy concentration, non-software projects still make up a substantial baseline: 38% of 2026's new checkout links belong to general services/consulting, 21% to courses and coaching, and 14% to ebooks, content, or community access.[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=It%20started%20climbing%20in%20March%202026%20and,sell%20ebooks%2C%20content%20or%20community%20access.%203.)

---

### 3. Rise of the "Product Factory" and Multi-Domain Portfolios
The data uncovers distinct behavioral patterns among active solo founders, many of whom are no longer building just one monolithic startup:
* **Product Factories:** Many indie developers now ship a brand-new single-purpose tool every week or two, utilizing free subdomains or separate properties while managing them under a single analytics and business backend.
* **Language and Industry Slicing:** A common tactic involves cloning a successful micro-tool across exact-match domains tailored for specific countries, languages, or vertical industries (e.g., deploying separate booking apps tailored strictly for kennels, hotels, and marinas).

---

### 4. The "Grey Side" of Checkout Links
Out of the 200,000 analyzed links, about **17,000 websites** shared checkout links that appeared across five or more distinct sites.[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=17%2C000%20websites%20carry%20a%20checkout%20link%20that,again%20as%20large%20as%20all%20of%202025.) The data categorizes these shared networks into three groups:
1. **Legitimate Hit Products:** Viral Mac utilities or developer tools widely recommended by directories and review blogs.
2. **Backlink Networks:** Programmatic template sites (such as dozens of auto-generated SEO or backlink checkers) cross-linking payment rails.
3. **Compromised Infrastructure:** Instances where payment links (such as legacy Gumroad setups for adult or gambling offers) were illicitly injected into hacked, dormant websites belonging to schools, local clinics, or cultural institutions.[jasonzhu.ai](https://jasonzhu.ai/en/blog/indie-payments-report-2026#:~:text=Gumroad%20links%20for%20gambling%20or%20adult%20products,the%20sites%20of%20schools%2C%20clinics%20and%20museums.)

---

The data reveals a dramatic shift away from traditional infrastructure toward newer developer-focused Merchants of Record (MoRs), an explosion of software and AI tooling, and unusual operational patterns among modern indie builders.

* **Dodo Payments:** **71%** of new sellers offer software, and **29%** sell AI products.
* **Polar:** **58%** software, **27%** AI products.
* **Creem:** **65%** software, **24%** AI products.

These newer alternatives are growing rapidly because they handle complex global tax/VAT compliance out of the box (acting as the Merchant of Record) and **accept founders from regions like mainland China** where traditional Stripe onboarding is restricted.

---

### 2. The 2026 Surge in Software and AI Products
The composition of what indie developers are building has shifted aggressively toward code and AI:
* **The Software Boom:** Throughout 2025, software hovered around 6% to 8% of new checkout links. By September 2026, software's share surged to **20%** (one in every five new sellers).

Despite this tech-heavy concentration, non-software projects still make up a substantial baseline: 38% of 2026's new checkout links belong to general services/consulting, 21% to courses and coaching, and 14% to ebooks, content, or community access.

2. **Backlink Networks:** Programmatic template sites (such as dozens of auto-generated SEO or backlink checkers) cross-linking payment rails.
